featured_reviews.review_text:
For those who genuinely enjoy tasty, fresh, and authentic ice cream, Naturals Ice Cream is a lovely location.
This store, which is well situated in the center of Cuffe Parade, continues the brand's tradition of providing fruit-based, preservative-free ice creams that are distinct from standard commercial options.

Naturals' dedication to quality and simplicity is what sets it apart. Real fruit flavors are immediately apparent in each scoop, which feels rich, creamy, and authentic.
In addition to being delicious, popular choices including Sitaphal, Mango, Anjeer, and Tender Coconut taste authentically handcrafted.

The sweetness is well-balanced and not overbearing, and the texture is silky.

This specific store has a tidy, light-filled, and welcoming atmosphere. The rapid service guarantees that you won't have to wait long, even at peak hours, and the open counter makes it easy for customers to observe the available flavors.
If you're not sure what to choose, the staff is always willing to provide samples and is courteous and helpful.

The constancy in quality is another excellent feature. The flavor and freshness are the same whether you arrive in the day or late at night. It's also a great place for a fast post-meal dessert stop or a laid-back adventure.
Ice cream fans should visit Naturals Ice Cream in Cuffe Parade. It stands out in Mumbai's bustling dessert market thanks to its emphasis on natural ingredients, distinctive tastes, and dependable quality. This place won't let you down if you prefer real flavors over fake ones.

featured_reviews.name: Ameeta mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Absolute Gold Standard for Natural, Fruit-Based Ice Cream. No Contest.

For decades, Naturals has been more than just an ice cream parlor—it’s a beloved Mumbai ritual. In a world of artificial flavors and creamy overload, Naturals stands apart by celebrating the true, intense essence of real fruit and ingredients. It’s the taste of purity and nostalgia, every single time.

The Ice Cream (5/5):
This is where magic happens. We tried the Sitaphal (Custard Apple), Tender Coconut, and the classic Chikoo. Each scoop was an explosion of authentic, unadulterated flavor. The Sitaphal was fragrant and loaded with real fruit pulp, the Tender Coconut was refreshing and creamy with delicate coconut pieces, and the Chikoo tasted like the fruit itself, perfectly sweet and earthy. The textures are superb—smooth yet substantial, never overly airy or gummy. You can taste the quality in every bite.

Ambiance & Service (4/5):
The outlets are typically bright, clean, and functional. It’s all about the ice cream, not lavish seating. The queue, especially on weekends, is a testament to its legendary status. Service is quick and efficient—the staff knows the menu inside out and are happy to offer samples if you’re undecided.

Heads Up:

Seasonal Specials are a MUST-try. If Jackfruit, Lychee, or Fig are available, don’t think twice.

It’s all vegetarian and uses real sugar, not artificial sweeteners. The purity is palpable.

Be prepared for a queue, but it moves fast and is 100% worth the wait.

This is not overly rich, buttercream-style ice cream. It’s lighter, fruit-forward, and uniquely refreshing.

Verdict:
Naturals Ice Cream isn't just the best in Mumbai; for its specific category of natural fruit ice creams, it’s arguably the best in India. It represents an unwavering commitment to quality that has never faltered. It’s the taste of childhood, summer, and sheer honesty in a cup. A perfect five-star experience that never disappoints. An absolute must-visit for anyone in the city.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Bono icecream used to be genuinely good when it started. The quality has fallen and how. I tried a "Bono bar" and I'm really questioning the ingredients listed on the package. After about 2 bites I had to throw the bar into the trash, it was that bad.

They claim they use Belgian chocolate in the ice cream and the shell. I would be interested to know what Belgian chocolate they are using, the shell tastes like they use cheap chocolate compound. How does this fancy boutique icecream taste WORSE than a Magnum bar?! Someone should do a lab test and verify their "honest ingredients" claim...

When I read the packaging to check the ingredients, I also noticed that it clearly says manufactured by Caro Rocher Pvt Ltd and MARKETED by Blue Cheese Boutique Ice Cream Pvt Limited. The Chesson sisters (aka Blue Cheese and the founders of Bono icecream) no longer manufacture their own ice cream, but merely market it. This probably explains the drop in quality.

Sad to see what was genuinely once a good homegrown brand go the same way as Theobroma, another example of how outsourcing production leads to a major drop in quality. No amount of "cheeky" slogans and Rolling Stones rip-off logos can make up for bad tasting food.

customer_updates.name: Gaurav Tayade
customer_updates.text:
K. Rustom & Co. is not just an ice cream parlour — it’s a slice of Mumbai’s history, nostalgia, and sweetness served between two wafer biscuits. Located right opposite Marine Drive, this humble little shop has been delighting generations of Mumbaikars long before fancy dessert chains took over the city. Walking into K. Rustom’s feels like stepping back in time, where simplicity, tradition, and genuine flavor still matter.
The moment you enter, you’re greeted by a display filled with colorful ice cream sandwiches stacked neatly in their signature paper wraps. There’s no loud décor, neon lights, or Instagram aesthetic — and that’s exactly the charm of this place. It has retained its old-world authenticity over the decades, focusing purely on what truly matters: great taste and generous portions at affordable prices.
The menu may look simple, but every flavor carries its own personality. From classic favorites like strawberry, vanilla, and chocolate to more unique ones like walnut crunch, rum and raisin, raspberry ripple, and kesar pista — each scoop has a distinct richness. The ice cream is perfectly firm, creamy yet light, and the wafer adds that satisfying crunch which makes every bite nostalgic.
One of my personal favorites is their Walnut Crunch — it’s rich, nutty, and has that perfect balance of sweetness without being overpowering. The Rum and Raisin flavor, too, stands out with its mature taste and smooth texture. Even their Mango and Pineapple flavors are fresh and fruity, reminding you of homemade ice creams made with love.
What makes K. Rustom’s truly special, though, is the experience that surrounds it. You grab your ice cream sandwich, step outside, and just a few steps away is the iconic Marine Drive promenade. Sitting by the sea, enjoying the breeze, and relishing that cold, creamy delight as waves crash nearby — it’s a feeling that no modern dessert café can replicate. It’s Mumbai in its purest form — simple joys in a chaotic city.
Another reason people love K. Rustom’s is their consistency. They’ve been serving quality ice creams for decades, and despite the growing popularity, they haven’t changed their style or pricing drastically. The service is quick, the staff polite, and everything runs with quiet efficiency — just like it always has.
If you’re visiting Mumbai or even if you’ve lived here all your life, K. Rustom & Co. deserves a spot on your must-visit list. It’s a reminder that some things never need to change to stay perfect.
In a world of gourmet desserts and Instagram cafés, K. Rustom’s remains refreshingly old-fashioned — and that’s exactly what makes it legendary. A scoop of nostalgia, a dash of heritage, and a lot of happiness — that’s what every visit feels like. ❤️

Visited the Colaba outlet on 15th December and enrolled in the Baskin Robbins rewards program after seeing an in-store poster that stated “Free scoop on your 2nd visit.”
No validity period or expiry condition was mentioned on the poster or communicated at the time of enrolment.

I returned on 26th January for my second visit and was denied the free scoop. At this point, the staff member informed me — for the first time — that the offer is valid only for 18 days from the first visit. This condition was communicated verbally at the counter, only when I attempted to redeem the offer.

To escalate the matter, the staff called the store owner, who reiterated the same validity condition and stated that if there was an issue, it should be taken up with Baskin Robbins directly. No resolution was offered at the store level.

Introducing material terms only at the time of redemption — and then redirecting customers to the brand — is not acceptable. Promotional offers that influence customer decisions must disclose all conditions clearly and upfront, not retroactively through verbal explanations.

The same poster also mentions rewards on every 5th visit, which reasonably creates the impression of an ongoing loyalty program rather than a narrowly time-restricted offer. This inconsistency adds to the confusion and dissatisfaction.

Sharing this review to seek clarity and accountability from the brand, and to highlight the need for transparent communication at store level.

From indulgent Belgian Chocolate and perfectly balanced Salted Caramel to refreshing Alphonso Mango and dreamy Madagascar Vanilla, every scoop feels artisanal and fresh, never overly sweet. Their signature creations, like “The Big Six,” combine fruits, nuts, and scoops into a visual and flavorful treat, while monthly experimental flavours keep things exciting. Though prices can add up and delivery sometimes struggles against Mumbai’s heat, the balance of authenticity, nostalgia, and innovation makes Bhide’s a true ice cream lover’s destination — a five-star gem worth every bite.
